fields.h1: Build Compliance Automation for the Work Between Audits

fields.features_heading: What a Compliance Team Stops Doing by Hand
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the reminders, reviews, and records your controls depend on as one app, on a database you own.
fields.feature_1:
Controls written as plain sentences

You write who acts, by when, and what counts as done, and Emergent builds the workflow from that prompt. A new rule is one more sentence in the next prompt, not a rebuild.
fields.feature_2:
Reviews that start from live data

The app reads accounts, vendors, and tickets from any tool with an API, such as Slack or HubSpot. A review opens on the current list instead of last month's spreadsheet export.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders on a timer, then escalation

Every task carries an owner and a due date. When one slips, the owner gets a Slack or email reminder, and after the number of days you choose, the request moves to their manager.
fields.feature_4:
Vendor documents read into fields

Upload a vendor's questionnaire or certificate, and the app reads it into structured fields with AI. A field it is unsure of goes to a person before anyone relies on that value.
fields.feature_5:
A record of who decided what

Each acknowledgment, approval, and revocation is saved to a database you own with a name and a time. An auditor's request becomes a filtered list, not a search of old inboxes.
fields.feature_6:
No cap on runs or approvers

Review every account and every vendor each quarter with no task cap and no per-approver seats. On a paid plan, the full code also exports to your own GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Compliance Checks to Automate First
fields.tab_content_1:
7 people still owe a sign-off after 5 days

Tessaline Labs publishes version 3 of its acceptable use policy. The app emails all 48 employees a link to read it and click Acknowledge, and logs each click with its timestamp. After 5 days, 41 have signed off, and the 7 who have not get a reminder in Slack.
fields.tab_content_2:
Managers confirm who keeps access, account by account

On the first business day of the quarter, the app sends each manager the accounts their team holds, read through each tool's API. Dov Halpern keeps 10 of his 12 and revokes 2 that belong to a contractor who left. Each decision is logged with his name and the date.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two No answers hold a vendor for security

A buyer requests a new vendor, Quillmate, and the app sends Quillmate a 20-question security questionnaire. Two answers come back No: background checks for staff and multi-factor sign-in. The request waits for the security lead, Anneliese Kamau. She approves or rejects it in the app.
fields.tab_content_4:
Evidence 3 days late copies in the compliance lead

Six weeks before the annual audit, the app assigns 18 evidence items to their control owners, each with a due date. By the deadline, 15 are uploaded and 3 are late. Each late owner gets a reminder, and once an item is 3 days past due, the compliance lead, Joaquin Ferrer, is copied in.

fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to map your recurring controls, then build and test compliance automation that runs them on schedule.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the controls you prove by hand
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the workflow in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every recurring control your team proves by hand, such as policy sign-offs or quarterly access reviews. Note how often each one runs and the hours it takes. Start with the one that costs the most time.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Assign every task to one named person with a due date. A shared inbox cannot be reminded. Pick a person, plus a backup for the weeks when that person is out.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe each workflow the way you would brief a new analyst, starting with the event that triggers it and ending with what counts as done. Emergent builds the app from that description.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Start with the employee list from your HR system. Policy sign-offs and access reviews both depend on who works at the company today, so a stale list breaks both.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick how many days a task can sit before its owner is reminded, and how many more before their manager hears about it. Keep the first reminder to one line with a link.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last quarter's records through the app before it goes live. Compare who it would have reminded with who ran late, and rewrite any rule that disagrees.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Check the log at quarter end
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the decision log at the end of each quarter and confirm every task has a name and a date against it. Any gap shows you which rule to tighten next.

faq_plan.q: What is compliance automation and how does it work?
faq_plan.ref: What is compliance automation and how does it work?

prov.original: What is compliance automation and how does it work?

faq_plan.a: Compliance automation is the process of using technology, AI included, to check systems for compliance continually. It works by replacing manual processes with software that tracks all compliance procedures in one location. The status of every control is then visible without a spreadsheet.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up compliance automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick one recurring control, write down who owns it and when it is due, then describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder. Emergent builds the app around that control, and you change a rule later by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing. Run one control for a full cycle before you add the next.

faq_plan.q: What is the best compliance automation software?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best compliance automation software?

prov.original: What is the best compliance automation software?

faq_plan.a: No single tool is best for every team, because a company preparing for a certification audit needs something different from one running daily control work. Vanta's product page says it continuously monitors your systems to make sure you stay compliant and secure. Compare compliance automation software on which frameworks it maps and which of your systems it can read.

faq_plan.q: What are the best compliance automation platforms?
faq_plan.ref: What are the best compliance automation platforms?

prov.original: What are the best compliance automation platforms?

faq_plan.a: The best platform is the one whose evidence your auditor accepts without rework. Start by asking your audit firm which compliance automation tools it works with. Drata, for one, creates a separate, centralized audit workspace for your auditor, complete with mapped evidence. Draft the policies themselves with document automation, from a template your team has approved.

faq_plan.q: What is compliance automation used for?
faq_plan.a: Compliance automation is used for the recurring tasks that show a control is working, such as tracking security training completion or recording the date each laptop is wiped after someone leaves. Emergent builds each of these as an app with no task cap, and a quarter with twice the reviews still runs every one.

DevSecOps compliance automation is the practice of running compliance checks inside the pipeline that builds and ships your software. IBM describes DevSecOps as an application development practice that automates the integration of security at every phase of the software development lifecycle. Set a failed check to hold the release until someone fixes it.

faq_plan.q: What are the tools that help with EU VAT compliance automation?
faq_plan.ref: what are the tools helpful in eu vat compliance automation
faq_plan.a: The EU's One Stop Shop lets a seller declare and pay VAT due in Member States where it is not established, through a web portal in the Member State where it is identified. Under the Union scheme, that return is submitted quarterly. Give each filing the draft-then-approve pattern of a content approval workflow before it goes in.

faq_plan.q: What is included in a compliance workflow?
faq_plan.a: A compliance workflow includes a trigger event, a named owner with a due date, and a recorded result, all for one control. For an employee exit, HR marks the last day, IT disables each account that day, and the manager confirms the list is empty. The app Emergent builds keeps every step's record in your own database, where the history stays if a tool changes.

faq_plan.q: What are the limits of compliance workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Its limits are the judgment calls: whether a vendor's No answer is acceptable, whether a policy exception is justified, or what to tell an auditor about a missed control. Let the automation gather the facts and route them, and keep each decision with a named person who can explain it later.

findings.quote: The free tier covers building and publishing, which lets you run one control for a full cycle before you add the next.
findings.issue: The approved claim (free-start) is only 'Free to start; the free tier covers building and publishing'. The added 'which lets you run one control for a full cycle' promises that a free app runs for a whole review cycle (a quarter, per the page), a claim about Emergent's free tier limits that is not in rules/capabilities.json. Only instance; FAQ 10 'Emergent is free to start' stays within the claim.
findings.fix: End at the ledger wording: 'The free tier covers building and publishing.' If a sentence is wanted, make it about the workflow, not the plan: 'Run one control for a full cycle before you add the next.'

findings.quote: The central tool is the EU's One Stop Shop.
findings.issue: The EC source supports only that the OSS schemes let a seller declare and pay VAT due in Member States where it is not established, through a portal in its Member State of identification. It does not call OSS the central tool of EU VAT compliance; OSS covers only those cross-border supplies, and domestic VAT returns are filed nationally. The first sentence of the answer overstates a third-party system.
findings.fix: Scope it to what the source says: 'For sellers charging VAT in EU countries where they are not established, the EU's One Stop Shop lets them declare and pay it through one web portal in the Member State where they are identified.' Keep the sourced quarterly line.
